claims.text: Argo CD is a GitOps agent that runs as Pods inside a Kubernetes cluster, compares manifests in a Git repository with the live objects and applies them; it does not build container images.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Overview (What is Argo CD, How it works); Core concepts

claims.text: Argo CD is installed by kubectl apply -n argocd of the install manifest (install.yaml) the Argo CD project publishes, into a namespace created first (install.yaml holds no Namespace); upgrading = applying the new version. Đơn Hàng pins a copy at deploy/argocd/install.yaml, 3.1.16.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Getting Started > Install Argo CD; Operator Manual > Upgrading > Overview; examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/argocd-install.sh:10-16

claims.text: Argo CD cannot be what installs itself the first time: before its Pods run, nothing in the cluster can apply it, so a tool outside it (argocd-install.sh with kubectl) applies it first.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Getting Started (install with kubectl); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/argocd-install.sh:10-12

claims.text: install.yaml (3.1.16) creates Deployments, Services, RBAC objects, 3 customresourcedefinitions; 6 Deployments (applicationset-controller, dex-server, notifications-controller, redis, repo-server, server) and statefulset argocd-application-controller, which keeps its Pod running like a Deployment.

After install, kubectl api-resources --api-group=argoproj.io lists applications, applicationsets, appprojects (argoproj.io/v1alpha1, namespaced); kubectl then gets/applies an Application like any built-in kind.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/argocd-install.txt; Kubernetes docs: Custom Resources; Argo CD docs: Declarative Setup

claims.text: argocd-repo-server keeps a local copy (cache) of the Git repository and reads the manifests under spec.source.path from it; argocd-application-controller compares the live state with the target state from Git.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Architecture overview / Components (Repository Server, Application Controller)

claims.text: Application spec: spec.project (the default project exists automatically); spec.source.repoURL, targetRevision, path; spec.destination.server, namespace. targetRevision can be a branch or a commit; main means the newest commit on main; path is a folder in the repository.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Operator Manual > Declarative Setup > Applications; Tracking and Deployment Strategies; User Guide > Projects (default project)

claims.text: destination.server https://kubernetes.default.svc is the API server's address from inside the cluster, i.e. the cluster Argo CD itself runs in (the in-cluster destination).
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Declarative Setup > Clusters (in-cluster, https://kubernetes.default.svc); Kubernetes docs: Accessing the API from within a Pod

claims.text: The Application object lives in the namespace argocd (where Argo CD is installed), not in its destination namespace; by default Argo CD reads Applications only from its own namespace.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Declarative Setup ('must be installed in the same namespace where Argo CD is installed'); Applications in any namespace (opt-in)

claims.text: An Application with no syncPolicy (staging-manual.yaml) does not apply manifests to the cluster by itself: Argo CD compares, and applies only when someone asks. Whether it applies by itself is set in the Application (syncPolicy.automated).
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: User Guide > Automated Sync Policy (manual sync is the default); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 deploy/gitops/lessons/staging-manual.yaml:5-6

claims.text: Only folders an Application points at are compared; envs/production in the same repository is not compared with staging because no Application in donhang-staging names it.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Declarative Setup > Applications (source.path); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/gitops-repo.sh (only apps/staging.yaml copied)

claims.text: git-server.yaml@stage-3: one Gitea Pod (Deployment gitea, 1 replica) in namespace git, repositories in an emptyDir (lost with the Pod), served at http://gitea.git.svc:3000, reachable only from Pods in the cluster.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 deploy/gitops/git-server.yaml; Kubernetes docs: Volumes > emptyDir; DNS for Services and Pods

claims.text: gitops-repo.sh@stage-3 applies git-server.yaml, creates admin user donhang, creates public repository donhang-config and pushes envs/ and apps/staging.yaml from deploy/gitops/config-repo as its first commit; the repo holds only YAML.
Argo CD can read a public Git repository over HTTP without configuring credentials; credentials are needed only for private repositories.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: User Guide > Private Repositories

claims.text: envs/staging/api.yaml@stage-3 names image ghcr.io/duyan11110/donhang-api:sha-<commit> pushed by CI; other images are pulled from public registries.

Try it: kubectl --context kind-donhang-staging apply -f deploy/gitops/lessons/staging-manual.yaml -o name prints application.argoproj.io/staging; get applications -n argocd lists staging; get pods -n argocd shows only argocd-* Pods.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/gitops-first-sync.txt (first lines); argocd-install.txt; Kubernetes docs: kubectl apply -o name

claims.text: kind names a cluster's kubeconfig context kind-<name> (kind-donhang-staging). argocd-install.sh:7 and scripts/lib/gitops.sh:7 (sourced by gitops-repo.sh) wrap kubectl with --context kind-donhang-staging, so both target that cluster whatever context is current.
claims.source_hint: kind docs: Quick Start > Interacting With Your Cluster; examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/argocd-install.sh:6-7, scripts/lib/gitops.sh:5-7, scripts/devops/gitops-repo.sh:12

claims.text: argocd-install.sh:14 `kubectl create namespace argocd --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -` succeeds whether or not the namespace exists; lines 17-18 `kubectl rollout status` wait until the Deployments and the StatefulSet have rolled out (timeout 600s).
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: kubectl create (--dry-run=client), kubectl apply, kubectl rollout status; examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/argocd-install.sh:14-18
